item.title: Could Grenada’s New Adults-Only Retreat Be Its Most Intimate Escape Yet?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Silversands Beach House on Grenada’s Portici Beach is entering a new chapter as an adults-only resort, now welcoming guests ages 16 and older. Set along a secluded stretch of the Caribbean coast, the intimate property has 28 accommodations designed around indoor-outdoor living, with staggered cliffside positioning, floor-to-ceiling windows and canopied terraces that open to uninterrupted views of the sea. The shift gives the resort a more defined focus on privacy, tranquility and intimate Caribbean escapes.

The experience extends beyond the setting. Guests can dine at Azzurro, where Italian cuisine meets Caribbean influences, exercise in the open-air gym or retreat to the Wellness Room for personalized holistic treatments. The adults-only Beach House also offers a contrasting experience to its sister property, Silversands Grand Anse, located a short shuttle ride away and continuing to welcome families with suites, private villas, a Kids’ Club, spa and multiple dining concepts. Silversands Beach House was also named a 2026 Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Awards Best of the Best winner, a designation awarded to the top 1% of hotels on the platform.

The Curated Take: The interesting part of this evolution is not simply that children are no longer part of the guest mix, but that the resort is using its secluded setting to sharpen its identity around privacy. With only 28 accommodations, cliffside views and a naturally intimate relationship between indoor and outdoor spaces, the new adults-only positioning aligns the property more closely with travelers seeking a quieter Caribbean experience. It also creates a useful distinction within the Silversands Collection itself, allowing the two Grenada properties to serve distinctly different styles of travel.

item.title: What If You Could Fall Asleep With Wolves Outside Your Window?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In Timmins, Ontario, Canada, getting away from it all can mean getting considerably closer to the wild. Set on 175 acres of Northern Ontario wilderness, Cedar Meadows Resort & Spa offers travelers a chance to trade screens and city noise for forests, wildlife and wide-open skies. But the resort’s most unusual escape takes that immersion a step further with its “Sleeping With the Wolves” experience, where guests stay in glass-front cabins overlooking a timber wolf habitat.

From the privacy of their cabins, travelers can watch the wolves move through the forest and listen for their howls after dark, creating an experience that feels far removed from conventional luxury accommodations. The setting also leaves room for a slower pace, whether that means spending time at the spa, exploring the resort’s grounds or simply sitting quietly and observing the landscape. Rather than placing wildlife behind a traditional viewing barrier, the glass-front cabins make the surrounding habitat part of the overnight experience.

The Curated Take: “Sleeping With the Wolves” is compelling because it redefines what a luxury escape can look like. The appeal is not excess or entertainment, but proximity, privacy and the feeling of witnessing something wild from an intimate vantage point. For travelers drawn to meaningful experiences, this is the kind of unusual overnight stay that can become the story of the journey itself.

item.title: What If Your Christmas Market Escape Came With a Thermal Spa?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For travelers seeking a quieter alternative to London during the holidays, Bath, England offers a festive escape built around historic streets, seasonal markets and the restorative tradition of its natural thermal waters. From November 26 through December 13, 2026, the city’s annual Christmas Market will fill the center with more than 170 illuminated chalets featuring festive food, handmade goods and personalized gifts, with sustainability woven into the market’s offerings. The cobbled streets and Georgian architecture provide an atmospheric setting for winter walks and mulled wine.

Just a five-minute stroll from the market, The Gainsborough Bath Spa offers a more restorative side of the season. The five-star hotel is the only property in Bath with access to the city’s natural thermal waters, incorporating them into its spa experience through pools and treatments. After exploring the Christmas market, travelers can return to the hotel to soak in the same thermal tradition that has made Bath a destination for wellness and bathing for centuries, creating a holiday itinerary that balances festive discovery with time to slow down.

The Curated Take: Bath works particularly well for travelers who want Christmas atmosphere without making the holiday entirely about crowds and spectacle. The combination of a historic English city, a thoughtfully curated market and access to natural thermal waters gives the experience a distinct rhythm. Rather than simply adding a spa day to a Christmas trip, Bath makes bathing part of the destination’s identity, giving a winter city break an unusually restorative dimension.

item.title: Jackson Pollock’s “Blue Poles” Comes to Perth
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
One of Australia’s most recognizable paintings will travel west in April 2027 when Jackson Pollock’s Blue Poles goes on display at the Art Gallery of Western Australia for the first time. On loan from the National Gallery of Australia, the nearly five-metre-wide 1952 painting is considered one of the country’s most significant artworks and is valued at more than $500 million. Its presentation in Perth will be accompanied by public programs, talks and community events.

Pollock’s radical poured-paint technique makes Blue Poles an especially striking work to encounter in person, where its scale and physicality become part of the experience. The exhibition also creates an opportunity for travelers to pair a major international art icon with Perth’s broader cultural scene and Western Australia’s distinctive landscape and design culture.

The Curated Take:
Some artworks are worth planning a trip around simply because photographs cannot replicate their scale or physical presence. Blue Poles is one of those works. Its arrival gives Perth a major cultural draw while offering travelers another reason to include the city’s museums and galleries in an itinerary.

item.title: What If Edinburgh Were Your Entire Holiday Season?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From Christmas markets and ice skating to fireworks and the legendary Hogmanay celebrations, Edinburgh, Scotland turns the winter season into an extended celebration. From November 14, 2026, through January 3, 2027, the Scottish capital will be filled with festive lights, carolers, seasonal treats and Yule logs, while the city’s Winter Festivals bring together Christmas markets, fairground rides and George Street’s Christmas Ice Rink. In East Princes Street Gardens, a traditional Christmas Market with approximately 70 stalls will sit beneath the city skyline, alongside the 46-meter-tall Big Wheel.

The season continues into the New Year with Edinburgh’s famous Hogmanay celebrations, including the Torchlight Procession, live music, fireworks and street food before the festivities culminate in a Street Party on Princes Street with Edinburgh Castle as its backdrop. For a stay that places travelers close to the action while offering a retreat from the crowds, The Glasshouse Hotel occupies a 160-year-old former church, transformed into a luxury boutique hotel with 77 rooms. Its two-acre rooftop garden provides panoramic views toward the city center and Calton Hill, creating a remarkably peaceful counterpoint to Edinburgh’s bustling winter calendar.

The Curated Take: Edinburgh’s appeal during the holidays is that the city itself becomes the experience. Travelers can move from historic streets and Christmas markets to the spectacle of Hogmanay without having to manufacture a festive atmosphere around their stay. The Glasshouse adds another layer through its combination of architectural history, contemporary luxury and a private-feeling rooftop garden, making it possible to experience Edinburgh’s celebrations while still having somewhere tranquil to retreat.

item.title: What If Christmas Came to Malaysia’s Tea Country?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
High in the Cameron Highlands of Malaysia, tea plantations, strawberry farms and glowing evening sunsets create an unexpected setting for a traditional Christmas escape. At Cameron Highlands Resort, a grand colonial-inspired retreat brings a nostalgic holiday atmosphere to the mountain landscape, where the cooler highland climate makes the season feel distinctly different from the tropical Malaysia travelers may expect.

Each winter, the resort transforms for the festive season with elaborate decorations throughout the property. Giant Christmas trees, garlands, mistletoe and stockings hung by the fire create an old-fashioned holiday setting, while the annual Christmas tree lighting marks the beginning of the celebrations. Beyond the resort, the Cameron Highlands offer a quieter landscape of tea estates and farms, giving travelers a chance to pair a festive stay with the region’s distinctive agricultural heritage and mountain scenery.

The Curated Take: There is something particularly appealing about a Christmas setting that feels transported from somewhere else. Cameron Highlands offers that contrast naturally: a tropical-country destination with cool mountain air, colonial-era character and a holiday atmosphere built around fireside nostalgia rather than snow. For travelers looking beyond conventional European Christmas markets and Alpine resorts, it is an intriguing way to experience the season through a very different cultural and geographic lens.

item.title: What If Lake Garda Has a Winter Side You’ve Never Seen?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Best known as a warm-weather escape, Lake Garda, Italy takes on a quieter character in winter, when snow arrives on nearby Monte Baldo and the towns around the lake turn toward Christmas markets and seasonal traditions. Monte Baldo offers seven ski lifts and 25 miles of snow-covered trails, giving travelers a chance to combine time on the slopes with the culture and scenery of one of northern Italy’s most celebrated lakes.

At Cape of Senses, an adults-only retreat perched about 600 feet above Lake Garda, winter days can move easily between mountain and lake. Guests can explore the “Natale tra gli Olivi” Christmas market as well as holiday markets in Bardolino and Lazise, or seek out the underwater Nativity display in Peschiera del Garda. Back at the hotel, après-ski, panoramic lake views and the 21,000-square-foot Senses Spa offer a slower counterpoint to a day outdoors, with the resort providing a warm retreat as the landscape settles into winter.

The Curated Take: Lake Garda’s winter appeal comes from the combination of experiences rather than any single seasonal attraction. Travelers can ski in the morning, explore Italian Christmas traditions in the afternoon and finish the day overlooking the lake from a sophisticated wellness retreat. For luxury travelers who already associate Garda with summer, winter presents a different rhythm, one that pairs Alpine activity with Italian culture and the pleasures of a lakeside escape.

item.title: What If You Experienced Japan After the Snow Fell?
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Japan in winter can feel like an entirely different country, and in the rural Aizu region of Fukushima Prefecture, snow transforms traditional villages, mountain valleys and rivers into a remarkably quiet landscape. Walk Japan’s five-day, four-night Onsen Gastronomy: Snowy Aizu tour takes travelers from Aizu-Wakamatsu to Inawashiro on a fully guided, easy snowshoeing journey through the western reaches of Japan’s Tohoku region, an area known for its history, traditional townscapes and natural beauty.

Each day brings a different perspective on the snow-covered countryside, from walking through mountain landscapes and rural villages to traveling alongside rivers beneath deep winter snow. The physical exploration is balanced by the restorative ritual of staying at Japanese inns and soaking in onsen, the country’s traditional hot spring baths. The journey culminates in Urabandai, where cobalt-blue lakes sit beneath the imposing presence of Mount Bandai, creating one of the region’s most striking winter landscapes.

The Curated Take: Aizu offers something increasingly difficult to find in Japan’s better-known destinations: the opportunity to experience the country at a slower pace and within a distinctly local landscape. Snowshoeing provides a way into the countryside, but the real appeal is the rhythm of the journey, where walking through winter scenery gives way to hot springs, traditional inns and regional culture. For travelers who already know Japan’s major cities, this is a compelling way to see a quieter side of the country without sacrificing the deeply Japanese experiences that make the journey memorable.

item.title: Casa Fuego Brings Fire and Mexican Flavor to Perth’s Northbridge
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Perth’s Northbridge has a new destination for Mexican food and cocktails with the August opening of Casa Fuego. The restaurant and bar is built around the flavors and energy of Mexico, with a menu featuring birria beef tacos, tostadas and burritos made with hand-pressed tortillas, slow-cooked meats and house-made salsa. The drinks program adds a cocktail-driven element to the experience.

Located in one of Perth’s cultural and dining hubs, Casa Fuego adds another international influence to a neighborhood already known for its lively restaurant scene. The focus on handmade tortillas, slow cooking and bold flavors gives the concept a culinary identity beyond the familiar shorthand of Mexican-inspired dining.

The Curated Take:
For travelers, the most interesting restaurant openings are often those that give a neighborhood another reason to explore it. Casa Fuego’s emphasis on handmade elements and fire-driven flavors makes it a natural addition to a Northbridge evening, particularly for visitors looking to experience Perth beyond its traditional sightseeing circuit.
